nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, this is the type of real numbers $\alpha$ that are algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$ and whose minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$ has degree at most $n$.
nodes.title: Real algebraic numbers of bounded degree

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a real number $\xi$, let $H(\alpha)$ denote the height of a real algebraic number $\alpha$. The classical exponent $\omega^*_n(\xi)$ is the supremum in $[0, \infty]$ of the set of real numbers $\omega > 0$ for which there are infinitely many real algebraic numbers $\alpha$ of degree at most $n$ with $0 < |\xi - \alpha| \le H(\alpha)^{-\omega - 1}$. It is $0$ when this set is empty.
nodes.title: Classical exponent of approximation by algebraic numbers

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a real algebraic number, let $p$ be its monic minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $D$ be the least common multiple of the denominators of the nonzero coefficients of $p$. The height $H(\alpha)$ is the largest absolute value of a coefficient of the integer polynomial $D p$. For a real number that is not algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$, the height is $0$.
nodes.title: Height of a real algebraic number

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\xi$ a real number, and $H(\alpha)$ the height of a real algebraic number $\alpha$. This is the set of real numbers $\omega > 0$ for which there are infinitely many real algebraic numbers $\alpha$ of degree at most $n$ with $0 < |\xi - \alpha| \le H(\alpha)^{-\omega - 1}$.
nodes.title: Approximation exponents admitting infinitely many solutions

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer and let $a = 1/(2 - \log 2)$. For every real number $\xi$ that is transcendental over $\mathbb{Q}$, the classical exponent of approximation to $\xi$ by real algebraic numbers of degree at most $n$ satisfies $\omega^*_n(\xi) \ge a n$.
